title: status readers B2: recovery tail, contention summary, and the remaining status readers (onboarding, handoff, bypass level, raw config validation, controlRootFor)
action: Split out of rust-port-14 (panel W8) so the gix mechanism risk sits alone. Port the non-git half of the status read spine: (1) RECOVERY/CONTENTION — readTranscriptTail bounded-window semantics (recovery.mjs:70, 64KB tail), the crash-candidate recovery block, and the contention summary over .bee/logs/contention.jsonl (busiest locks, worst wait); the transcript root is taken from the injected fixture root (rust-port-19 generates one at the exact encoded-project-dir path detectCrashCandidates resolves, with a heartbeat-stale session and a 300KB transcript), never the host $HOME. (2) THE READERS PANEL B2 FOUND WITH NO HOME, all called by buildStatus and none ported yet: readOnboarding (state.mjs:1797), readHandoff (state.mjs:1121), bypassLevel (state.mjs:1921 — gate_bypass / gate_bypass_level), readRawConfigForValidation (bee.mjs:600, feeding both validators). NOTE (corrected by rust-port-16's disclosed deviation): controlRootFor does NOT live in crates/bee-core/src/workspace.rs — it is in crates/queen-bee/src/adapter.rs, a binary-crate concern bee-core cannot depend on. Follow the pattern rust-port-16 established: take an already-resolved control_root parameter rather than re-deriving it inside bee-core (same 'supplied by caller' shape as guards.rs's WriteTopology). (3) THE REMAINING STATE HELPERS: importable — isKnownPhase (state.mjs:54), validateModelsConfig (state.mjs:422), validateAgentFilesDrift (state.mjs:669), hasStaleAdvisorKey (state.mjs:1954), classifySource (source-identity.mjs:50); NOT exported, private to bee.mjs — buildRecoveryBlock (:457), buildContentionSummary (:673), buildLaneRows (:471), buildLaneSummary (:496), computeRuntimeDrift (:527), findRepoHive (:580), ungrantedWorktreeNotice (:615). ORACLE SPLIT accordingly: importable units get import-style file-based node drivers (pattern of record: crates/bee-core/tests/fsutil_oracle.rs); the seven bee.mjs-private helpers are oracled through the WHOLE-COMMAND driver `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json`, diffed sub-object by sub-object — never a hand-invented oracle. NON-DETERMINISM FIXTURES (panel W6/W7), each named: clock-boundary reservation expiry (bee.mjs:741-746) and heartbeat staleness (claims.mjs:367) pinned by a frozen/injected clock rather than wall time; and the JS REFERENCE-IDENTITY filter at bee.mjs:744-746 (expiredUnreleased excludes by reference, not value) — include a fixture with an expired reservation deeply equal to an active one, where a value-equality port misclassifies. ALL tests in ONE target status_readers_b2.

truths: cargo --test status_readers_b2 runs and reports at least 15 passed, output listing fixture names per class
every ported reader matches its mjs oracle on the same fixtures; the seven bee.mjs-private helpers match the corresponding sub-objects of the real bee.mjs status --json
recovery tail reads the injected transcript root from the grown fixture (hermetic, never host $HOME) and matches mjs output on a non-degraded recovery block
the reference-identity reservation fixture passes (deeply-equal expired vs active not misclassified), and clock-boundary fixtures are pinned, not wall-time dependent

trace.outcome: Rework round (goal-check NEEDS_REVISION, 9/11 checks passed): closed the 2 test-only gaps. (1) read_raw_config_for_validation is now oracle-diffed via the whole-command status --json staleness_warnings config-validate line across all three shapes (Absent / Value(null)-malformed / Value(object)-present). (2) The reservation reference-identity fixture gained a second, sharper case with two leases projecting to DEEPLY EQUAL LeaseReservationView rows (same resource, no acquired_at, only expires_at differs and is dropped by the projection), proving the bug defeats even a value-equality dedup, not just distinguishable rows -- and the misleading 'deeply equal' claim on the original fixture's comment was corrected to describe what it actually proves (a distinguishable-rows case). Both auto-fix deviations from the first pass (read_lane's missing created_at:null default merge, build_lane_rows' spurious workers:[] leak) are now recorded as structured cell deviations per the judge's bookkeeping note.

deviations.issue: read_lane deserialized lane records into the shared State struct without merging laneRecordFrom's defaultLaneRecord created_at: null default, so a lane file written without a created_at key produced no created_at field at all instead of an explicit null -- diverging from the real mjs readLane/laneRecordFrom output.
deviations.fix: read_lane now injects created_at: null into the deserialized State's extra map when the source JSON omitted it, scoped to lane reads only (never state.json's read_state, whose own defaultState() has no created_at key at all).
deviations.found_by: oracle-diffing build_lane_rows against the real `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json --lanes-full` output on a hand-built two-lane fixture.

deviations.issue: build_lane_rows serialized the shared State struct directly, which always carries a workers: [] field (state.json's defaultState() default) even though no real .bee/lanes/<feature>.json record -- nor laneRecordFrom's defaultLaneRecord -- ever has a workers key.
deviations.fix: build_lane_rows now removes the workers key from each lane's serialized JSON before adding bound_sessions, matching the real mjs --lanes-full array exactly.
deviations.found_by: same oracle diff as the created_at deviation above, same fixture.

Driver imports the real frozen .bee/bin/lib/{state,source-identity,reservations}.mjs and execFileSyncs the real bee.mjs status --json; no hand-written reimplementation. Literal asserts are extra pins alongside oracle equality, never substitutes. Sole no-oracle case (ungranted_worktree_notice, mjs re-derives process.cwd()) byte-compared by the judge itself: equal.

read_raw_config_for_validation (crates/bee-core/src/state.rs:476) has exactly one hit in the whole workspace - its own definition. No test calls it; every validator test hand-builds RawConfig::Value/Absent. Truth #2 (every ported reader matches its mjs oracle) unmet for the reader the action names explicitly (bee.mjs:600). Logic matches mjs by inspection; the gap is proof, not correctness. Secondary: ungranted_worktree_notice asserts only prefix + 2 substrings, so a mid-string divergence would slip.

Fixture built via queen-bench --generate; injected root <fixture>/fixture-transcripts in .bee/config.json recovery.transcript_roots with a >=300KB transcript, never host $HOME. Tail window 262144 == recovery.mjs:49; contention window 65536 == bee.mjs:669. Rust side uses parameterized claude_projects_root_with(env, home); env-reading variant never called from tests.

PINNED_NOW_MS drives both boundary tests; lease expiry proves the <= edge both ways against the real listReservations oracle with the same pinned now; heartbeat staleness likewise. Only wall-clock use is documented and forced by mjs resolveSessionId calling Date.now() with no override.

The two leases at status_readers_b2.rs:676-725 differ in resource path, workflow_id, workspace_id and timestamps - not the deeply-equal expired/active pair truth #4 and the cell action both name, and the test's own comment at :719-721 claims a deep-equality property the fixture does not exercise. It still discriminates a value-equality port (2 vs 1), so the operational purpose holds, but weaker than specified. Judge constructed the specified fixture in /tmp (identical resource path, no acquired_at, expires_at 2020 vs 2099 - identical projected rows) and ran the real frozen CLI there: '2 reservation(s) expired but never released'. Missing test is ~12 lines, no production change.

bee.mjs:739-743 filters with active.includes(r) over two separately-mapped arrays, so the identity test is always false; confirmed end-to-end by running the real CLI on a one-expired/one-active fixture ('2 reservation(s) expired but never released'). reservations.rs:275-277 reproduces it and documents it as deliberate under D1 in a 20-line comment quoting the mjs source. Consistent with D1 (CONTEXT.md:21) and D3 (CONTEXT.md:23).

git show --stat 3eae3a8 touches only .bee/cells/rust-port-20.json and crates/bee-core/{src,tests}/* - no .bee/bin/, no packages/bee/, no crates/Cargo.toml. No subprocess in any ported reader (only pre-existing std::process::id and thread::spawn in fsutil.rs). control_root is a parameter on session_has_active_claim, detect_crash_candidates, build_recovery_block, build_lane_summary; no controlRootFor implementation exists in bee-core, only doc references stating the caller supplies it (rust-port-16 pattern). resolved_session_id is likewise a parameter, not re-derived.

guard_support.rs 16+/2-: both hunks forced by Session gaining named lane/transcript_path fields. The round-trip assertion went from one line to two and now pins BOTH the named field and the absence of the shadowed extra key - a strengthening, not a weakening. No assertion deleted or loosened. No Session serialization path exists in bee-core or queen-bee, so no 'lane': null can leak to disk.

(1) created_at: defaultLaneRecord carries created_at: null and laneRecordFrom merges it under the parsed record, so mjs readLane always returns the key - Rust read_lane now injects it. (2) workers: defaultLaneRecord has no workers key and buildLaneRows spreads the record whole, so the State struct's serde-default empty vec was spurious - removed only inside build_lane_rows, State itself untouched. Both proven by full-record equality against the real --lanes-full array. No regressions: cargo test -p bee-core 170 passed across all targets, clean build.
